flags.issue: LR3's 20 µs is the median, measured on a cloud Xeon VM with a non-real-time kernel. The repo's own results/logs/timing.log shows a p99.9 of about 168 µs, a max of about 4 ms and 0.13% missed deadlines. Calling a median 'per real-time update' invites a real-time C++ team (Apptronik L02) to open that log and challenge it, because real-time reviewers judge worst case, not median. Giving the statistic without saying which one reads as not knowing the difference.
flags.fix: Write '~20 µs median per 1 kHz update (of a 1 ms budget)', per LR3, and drop 'real-time'. needs Troy: to tell a real-time story, add to FACTS the p99 of 60 µs and the SCHED_FIFO / mlockall / absolute-deadline benchmark (quadruped-eskf/cpp/apps/bench_loop.cpp, results/timing.json).

Spell out LR9: 'QP force-balance controller (fed ground truth) tracked velocity to 0.091 vs 0.169 m/s for the scripted trot; fed the estimate after a 4 s startup turn, 0 falls in 5 × 60 s walks.'

flags.issue: The page tags C++ by language standard (C++17) and nothing more. It shows no design or performance depth: nothing on memory, task structure, interrupts, concurrency or algorithmic cost. The repo has that depth: no heap use in orthosis_core.h, a FreeRTOS task pinned to core 1 with xTaskDelayUntil, serial output in its own task so printing can't delay the loop, an IRAM-safe encoder ISR that reads GPIO registers directly, encoder edge-timing speed estimation (under 0.02% error vs 12–111% for per-tick counting), and an ESKF predict that exploits the structure of F (O(15²·n) instead of O(n³)) and is parity-tested against the dense version. None of it is in FACTS, so none of it can appear.
flags.fix: Truthful now: use OR2's '1 kHz FreeRTOS task' and OR5's hardware-free core and CI cross-compile (see the flags above). needs Troy: promote to FACTS, from firmware/README.md and quadruped-eskf/README.md, (a) the pinned 1 kHz task with serial isolated in a separate task, (b) the IRAM ISR with edge-timing velocity estimation, and (c) the O(15²·n) structured covariance predict. One clause of any of these does more for C++ depth than the whole skills line.

top3: The code link doesn't reach any code. The Pages site has no GitHub link, and Pages serves only /docs. Switch to github.com/tmayer2112-ui/Troy_Mayer (H2) as a real hyperlink, and clean the repo before reviewers land there (needs Troy): root README, images moved to assets/, __pycache__ untracked, CI for quadruped-eskf.

The page hides its best software-engineering facts and misplaces the one it shows. Put OR5 on the controller bullet (hardware-free core host-tested against a simulator; 26 GoogleTest tests plus the ESP32-S3 build in CI) instead of hanging the 26 tests on the EMG estimator. Put BD6 (bit-identical regression checks before landing every change) in place of the in-progress MuJoCo clause.

The real-time and C++ framing claims more than the repo shows. '~20 µs per real-time update' is a median on a non-real-time VM (timing.log: max about 4 ms, 0.13% missed deadlines). The controllers that run 'on the estimate' are Python and use the Python filter. The ESP32 firmware has never run on the board. Rescope ('~20 µs median of the 1 ms budget', 'for an ESP32-S3'), and move the C++ projects above the Python-data research roles so the page doesn't read as a mechanical engineer who scripts.
